chunks: Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from Abdullah ibn al-Salt, from Yunus, from Sama'ah, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
Indeed, Allah, Mighty and Majestic, delegated all of His affairs to the Believer, but did not delegate to him that he humiliate himself.
Have you not seen the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic, here?
And to Allah belongs the Honour, and to His Messenger, and to the Believers.
And the Believer ought to be honourable (aziz) and not be humiliated (dhil).
ai.seo_question: What is the theological basis for a Muslim maintaining dignity and avoiding self-humiliation?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) clarifies that divine delegation (fawd) to the believer encompasses all affairs except self-humiliation, establishing a theological basis for preserving personal dignity (izzah). By citing Quran 63:8, the Imam links the believer's social and spiritual status to the ultimate source of honour, emphasizing that maintaining self-respect is a religious obligation rather than mere personal preference. This principle is foundational in Shia jurisprudence for determining when to accept hardship versus when to avoid unnecessary disgrace.
